A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revised layout and appendix numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original clustering experiments across 26 datasets, including fine-tuning, background sensitivity, label granularity, and encoder-evaluation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original clustering experiments and reports revised granularity results and additional aggregate statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark pipeline, encoders, and training objectives remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds deployment recommendations that extend the procedure: select an unknown-count agglomerative-clustering threshold by maximizing UMAP-space silhouette, and use K-Means or subset fitting when memory is insufficient. These are recommendations, not demonstrated changes to the benchmark runs.

E1.justification: All 26 clustering datasets remain. However, the auxiliary kNN classification-probing evaluation in v1 Appendix P disappears, and the reported BIOSCAN-1M granularity sweep in Figure 2 no longer includes tribe-level labels.

E2.justification: The auxiliary comparison with weighted kNN probing at five k values is removed with v1 Table 26. The main supervised, self-supervised, randomized, raw-image, and clustering comparators remain unchanged. DINOv2, SCAN, and TEMI receive discussion rather than new evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 2 switches from standard AMI to AMItrue, and Table 2 adds a relative background-gap metric. Appendix E.6 revises the reported BIOSCAN-1M HDBSCAN minimum cluster size from the stated default of 5 to 2. The retained result tables do not establish rerunning; the main splits, preprocessing, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The entire kNN-versus-clustering analysis supporting evaluation complementarity is removed, while the granularity analysis is substantially revised through AMItrue. Background sensitivity gains relative-gap quantification. The new fine-tuning appendix primarily redisplays an existing comparison and does not establish an additional ablation.

E5.justification: V2 adds pooled model-by-dataset paired t-tests across the central SSL and fine-tuning comparisons, reporting sample counts, effect sizes, and significance annotations. V1 primarily reports individual-model tests and explicitly specifies Bonferroni correction; that correction is no longer stated in v2. The documented seeds and run practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces intermediate-granularity AMI peaks with generally declining AMItrue curves; this is a changed metric, not a same-setting performance gain. V2 adds aggregate findings, including a 4.1-percentage-point far-OOD SSL advantage excluding MAE, and relative background gaps. V1's kNN correlations of 0.33–0.54 disappear. Numerical entries in Tables 7–25 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds the formal AMItrue definition, normalizing by true-label entropy after chance adjustment. It also corrects the silhouette numerator from a_i minus b_i to b_i minus a_i. These are substantive definition corrections and additions, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 introduces an explicit contribution claiming degradation with finer label granularity, corroborating Cole et al.; v1 instead reports intermediate-level peaks that contrast with that work. The explicit kNN-orthogonality contribution and concluding claim are removed, although a general orthogonality claim remains in the abstract. The principal domain-transfer claims are retained.

C2.justification: The granularity interpretation changes under the new normalization, from an intermediate-level preference to agreement with declining fine-grained performance. New practical guidance qualifies silhouette-based performance estimation as unvalidated, and Appendix B acknowledges that absolute AMI is not calibrated for dataset difficulty. V2 also explains HDBSCAN's conditional usefulness when rejected samples are excluded.

D1.justification: Appendix G corrects total fine-tuning compute from 11 to 22 GPU-days while retaining two A40 GPUs and approximately 43 hours per run. Table 6 newly explains the 48-hour timeout behind DNF entries, and Appendix E removes a contradictory duplicate Spectral Clustering parameter entry. Code and checkpoint access remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds representation-quality literature from Kalibhat, Garrido, Agrawal, and Lu, plus TEMI, and develops comparisons with CLID and Cole et al. It also explains the exclusion of broader-data encoders and learned clustering methods. This is a focused expansion of the retained SSL and clustering positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Practical Guidance section and appendix contents, expands the introduction and scope explanations, replaces the kNN appendix with a fine-tuning visualization appendix, and copyedits terminology and prose. The overall narrative sequence and most methodological and appendix text remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, Figures 1 and 3 gain significance markers, new Figure 6 displays fine-tuning differences, Table 2 gains a relative-gap column, and old Table 26 is removed. Journal formatting changes the title page, headers, typography, and spacing, while most existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Corrected metric definitions, explicit granularity normalization, clearer effect-size reporting, and practical guidance improve internal consistency and usability. The main benchmark evidence remains stable. Removing the kNN analysis weakens support for the abstract's retained orthogonality claim, and multiple-testing correction is less clearly documented; these tradeoffs limit the overall gain.
